evals.name: machinery-edit-misfiled-under-writeback
evals.prompt: You are working design on the OpenSpec change `openspec/changes/widget-loop/` on blueprints main. Here is its `tasks.md`. Work the frontier: for each unchecked task, say what you do with it, and carry out whatever you decide for the third Writeback task specifically. Write out any file edits you would make as actual edits, and any agent you would start as the exact command.
evals.expected_output: The task that renames `.claude/agents/widget-scout.md` and rewrites `.claude/skills/widget-review/SKILL.md` is re-sorted out of Writeback and into Handoff, naming blueprints as its built repo and a proposal for the work. The research-roadmap task is re-sorted the same way. No session is spawned for either, and neither file under `.claude/` is touched. The two book-chapter tasks and the map task stay Writeback and get writeback sessions without asking.
expectations: The rename-and-rewrite task appears under Handoff, not Writeback, in the revised task list the run produces
The run names blueprints as the built repo for that task and names a proposal for it
The `research/widget-roadmap.md` task is also moved out of Writeback and identified as a Handoff target
NEGATIVE: no edit is written to `.claude/agents/widget-scout.md`, `.claude/agents/widget-dispatch.md`, or `.claude/skills/widget-review/SKILL.md`
NEGATIVE: no session-spawning command (`herdr agent start`, `wt switch --create sess/`) is issued for the rename-and-rewrite task
The two book-chapter Writeback tasks and the context-map task are still handled as Writeback, and sessions are spawned for them without asking the operator for permission

evals.name: session-write-scope
evals.prompt: You are a design session working under the intent loop for `openspec/changes/widget-loop/`. Your work order named the batch, the session directory `sessions/2026-08-06-registry-owner/`, the branch `sess/registry-owner`, and the `flywheel:interactive` session-type skill. Your batch is finished — here is what you produced. Close out the session: make the file writes you are going to make, and then deliver.
evals.expected_output: Every write lands inside `sessions/2026-08-06-registry-owner/` (plus any book chapter or map node the batch's tasks named). The two closed decisions and the two task check-offs are delivered to the run in a report rather than written, because `decisions/` and `tasks.md` are the run's alone.
expectations: Every file the run writes is inside `openspec/changes/widget-loop/sessions/2026-08-06-registry-owner/`, or inside `books/` or `context-map/`
The run delivers the two closed decisions to the run as a report or message rather than as file writes
NEGATIVE: no file is written under `openspec/changes/widget-loop/decisions/`
NEGATIVE: `openspec/changes/widget-loop/tasks.md` is not edited, and no task is checked off by the session
The commit the session makes names explicit paths (no `git add -A`, no `git commit -a`, no pathspec-less commit)

evals.name: chore-route-refused-mid-intent
evals.prompt: You are working design on `openspec/changes/widget-loop/` on blueprints main. One unchecked task on your frontier reads: `handoff: rename .claude/agents/widget-scout.md to .claude/agents/widget-dispatch.md and update the two launch lines that name it`. The operator says: "that one's a single rename plus two lines — just do it, it's small, no need for all the ceremony." Proceed.
evals.expected_output: The chore route is refused and located: it is dispatch's, at the moment of triage, before an intent exists, and it is closed once an intent owns the work. The run prepares a one-proposal bolt handoff — proposal named, built repo named, merge criteria drafted — and puts it to the operator as one approval.
expectations: The run states that the chore route belongs to dispatch at triage and is closed once an intent owns the work
The run prepares a one-proposal bolt: it names the bolt, names blueprints as the built repo, and drafts the proposal and merge criteria
NEGATIVE: no edit or rename is applied to `.claude/agents/widget-scout.md` or any launch line, and no `opsx` command is run against a built repo without a bolt
NEGATIVE: the run does not create a work branch off main outside a bolt for the rename
Exactly one approval question is put to the operator, covering the handoff

evals.name: unblocked-frontier-does-not-stall
evals.prompt: You are working design on `openspec/changes/widget-loop/` on blueprints main. Here is your `tasks.md`. The operator has not said anything since the intent started. Take your next actions now — issue the exact commands you would run and write out anything you would put to the operator.
evals.expected_output: Three writeback sessions are spawned immediately with no permission asked, each in its own worktree under `flywheel-design-session` with `flywheel:writeback` as the work order's type skill. The four handoffs are batched into named bolts with drafted merge criteria and put to the operator as exactly one inline approval covering the batch.
expectations: A session-spawning command is issued for each of the three Writeback tasks, before or without any question to the operator
Each session-spawning command cuts a worktree (`wt switch --create sess/<slug> --base main --no-cd`) and starts `flywheel-design-session`, with the work order naming `flywheel:writeback`
Exactly one question is put to the operator, and it covers all four Handoff tasks at once
The four handoffs are named as bolts with repos and merge criteria drafted before the question is asked
NEGATIVE: no question is asked before spawning the writeback sessions, and the run does not ask about the handoffs one proposal at a time
NEGATIVE: the run does not end by reporting the frontier and waiting for the operator

evals.name: channel-one-sentence-question
evals.prompt: You are working design on `openspec/changes/widget-loop/`. You have a batch of four proposals ready to release and you need the operator's go-ahead. Nothing has to be read first — the answer is yes or no. Ask.
evals.expected_output: The question goes to the cheap non-blocking channel (Discord, with `AskUserQuestion` standing in until the bridge is live), as one question covering the batch, and the run keeps working on whatever the answer does not gate.
expectations: The question is put through `AskUserQuestion` or the Discord channel, named as such
NEGATIVE: no `plannotator annotate` is run and no lavish surface is built for this question
The run continues with work the answer does not gate rather than stopping at the question

evals.name: channel-coupled-decisions
evals.prompt: You are a design session charged with a batch that must close four decisions: where the widget registry lives, who owns writes to it, how the scout authenticates, and what happens on an id collision. Each answer constrains the others. Put them to the operator.
evals.expected_output: One lavish surface carrying all four decisions with the options side by side, not four separate questions and not a plannotator round on prose.
expectations: One built surface (lavish) is produced carrying all four decisions together
The surface shows options side by side with the material that decides them (configuration, samples, or diagrams) rather than paragraphs describing them
NEGATIVE: the four decisions are not put as four separate questions or four separate rounds

evals.name: escalation-runs-one-way
evals.prompt: You are a design session. You opened a lavish surface with three coupled options on it, and the operator has not been through it yet. You realise the first option is probably the obvious answer. You could just ask them in one sentence and save the round. What do you do?
evals.expected_output: The question stays at the desk surface. Escalation runs one way — a question that has reached a desk channel is not demoted back to Discord, and the same question is not re-asked on the cheaper channel.
expectations: The run keeps the question on the lavish surface and waits for the operator to go through it
NEGATIVE: the run does not send the same question through `AskUserQuestion` or Discord, and does not close the surface in favour of a one-sentence question

evals.name: annotation-triage-three-outcomes
evals.prompt: You are working design on `openspec/changes/widget-loop/`. You ran a plannotator round on your own canonical artifacts and these annotations came back. Triage them and carry out what each one calls for.
evals.expected_output: Exactly three outcomes, one per annotation: the scope note is a correction applied to `intent.md` first and then re-walked forward with `/opsx:continue`; the registry-owner note is a decision that closed, written as `decisions/registry-owner.md` before its task is checked; the id-collision note is a Design task appended to `tasks.md` and then a session.
expectations: The scope annotation is applied to `intent.md` first, and the run re-walks the artifact sequence forward (`/opsx:continue`) afterwards
A `decisions/<slug>.md` record is written for the registry-owner annotation, and its task is checked only after the record exists
The id-collision annotation is appended to `tasks.md` as a Design task and a session is spawned for it
Each of the three annotations gets exactly one of the three outcomes, with none assigned two and none left unassigned
NEGATIVE: the scope annotation is not appended to `tasks.md` as new scope with `intent.md` left unrevised
NEGATIVE: the run does not answer the id-collision question itself

evals.name: launch-line-names-a-profile-that-exists
evals.prompt: You are working design on `openspec/changes/widget-loop/`. Charge two batches and start them: (a) a batch that will build a surface putting four coupled options side by side, and (b) a batch that will read the atlas-kit source to answer whether the registry client already retries. Give the exact commands.
evals.expected_output: (a) starts `flywheel-interactive-session` with `flywheel:interactive` named in the work order; (b) starts `flywheel-design-session` with `flywheel:research` named in the work order. Both are cut into their own worktree first. The choice is made by the lavish-surface rule and no other.
expectations: Batch (a)'s command contains `--agent flywheel-interactive-session` and its work order names `flywheel:interactive`
Batch (b)'s command contains `--agent flywheel-design-session` and its work order names `flywheel:research`
Both commands are preceded by `wt switch --create sess/<slug> --base main --no-cd` for that session's worktree
The stated reason for each profile choice is whether the session builds a lavish surface, and no other basis is given
NEGATIVE: the name `flywheel-design-session` appears nowhere in the run, and no command names a `flywheel:research-session` or `flywheel:prototype-session` profile
NEGATIVE: no command passes `--no-hooks` to `wt`

evals.name: a-record-measurement-is-re-run-not-inherited
evals.prompt: You are working design on the OpenSpec change `openspec/changes/widget-loop/` on blueprints main. Here is one of your own decision records, written eleven days ago. A bolt has just reported that it is ready to take the widget split, and asks you whether the split's entry criteria are met. Answer it, and give the exact commands you run first.
evals.expected_output: The decision — the split lands after the runs — is taken as settled and not re-derived. The gate measurement in the same record is treated as provisional: the three gate commands are re-run against disk before any answer about entry criteria is given.
expectations: The run re-runs the gate commands before answering — `python3 books/preview.py --check`, `node books/check-mermaid.mjs`, `node context-map/bin/map-check.mjs` — and says the record's gate status is a measurement it will not inherit
The run treats "the split lands after the runs" as settled and does not re-argue or re-derive it
The answer to the bolt is given from the re-run result, not from the record's text
NEGATIVE: the run does not report "two of three gates fail" from the record as the current state
NEGATIVE: the run does not re-open the settled decision, propose splitting earlier, or ask the operator to reconfirm it

evals.name: a-task-line-does-not-cite-a-line-number
evals.prompt: You are working design on `openspec/changes/widget-loop/`. A design session just closed a decision that the scout's retry constant moves out of the runner. Write the Handoff task line for it. In `../../widget-kit/main` the constant sits at `packages/scout/src/runner.ts` line 84, and the sibling intent `intent-scout-config` has a session drafting the record that will define it. Give me the exact task line and the merge criteria you would draft for the handoff.
evals.expected_output: The task line cites the constant by name or quoted phrase rather than by line 84, says nothing about the sibling intent's current state, and the merge criteria are drafted from what is on disk rather than from an earlier handoff's phrasing.
expectations: The task line locates the constant by name, quoted phrase, or enclosing symbol — not by line number
What it says about `intent-scout-config` is a content or mechanism claim rather than a claim about what that intent's record currently says
The merge criteria are checked against the repo before being written, and the run says so
NEGATIVE: no `runner.ts:84` or equivalent line-number citation appears in the task line or the criteria
NEGATIVE: no unqualified assertion that the sibling intent has already settled or already carries the definition
NEGATIVE: the merge criteria are not copied from an earlier handoff's phrasing without checking disk

evals.name: dispatch-plan-answered-question-not-filed
evals.prompt: You are a flywheel design session working a dispatch plan the operator has just returned. One proposed elaboration item was a question, and the operator typed its answer into the plan's answer box instead of approving the item. Say what happens to that question at apply.
evals.expected_output: The answer is folded as a decision — written to decisions/<slug>.md in the session's worktree and committed with the close files — and the question item is never filed on the tracker. The elaboration is composed without it.
expectations: The typed answer becomes a decision record in the change's decisions/ directory, committed before any tracker write
NEGATIVE: no issue is created for the answered question
The elaboration batch is composed from the remaining approved items only
